column1: # Mutation sweep -- does the suite still catch each fix's defect at HEAD?
# Method: worktree at HEAD, revert the fix (or apply mutations/<finding>.patch),
# run the module, compare against the all-green CONTROL run. Every row MEASURED,
# nothing predicted. The control at f667f74 is 13/13 PASS, 0 cex and 0 UNREACHABLE
# everywhere, so any red below is caused by the mutation.
# "Baseline" is NOT this. In this project it means the pre-verification RTL at
# 61f0575 -- see formal/baseline/MANIFEST.tsv, a different measurement with a
# different question. Nothing in this file uses the word.
# class   rtl | harness   WHAT is being mutated.
#         Fifteen rows mutate the DESIGN and ask whether the instrument still
#         sees the defect. F-14 is the only row that mutates the INSTRUMENT and
#         asks whether it is load-bearing at all -- and that is the effort's own
#         thesis, so the column exists to keep the distinction visible rather
#         than to sort the file. F-14 and F-28 are a matched pair: identical
#         verdict shape (asserts all green, a cover goes unreachable), one from
#         the design side and one from the instrument side.
# head    the HEAD each row's outcome was MEASURED at.
#         The sweep runs at current HEAD by design -- "does the suite still catch
#         this" is a question about the code as it stands, not a historical
#         replay. So as HEAD moves past a row's recorded one the driver WARNS but
#         still runs, and a changed outcome is then a real result rather than
#         drift. Use `regress.sh --replay ...` to rebuild a row at the HEAD it
#         was recorded at, which is what makes the numbers below reproducible
#         rather than merely dated.
# method  revert | patch
# expect  cex:<leaf>            named property must be in the counterexample list
#         cover-unreachable     one or more covers must come back UNREACHABLE (vacuity)
#         elab-fail:<code>[:<n>]  the run must die BEFORE the property table, citing
#                               <code>; with <n>, exactly n distinct matching lines.
#                               harness-gate is the same class with the
#                               multiply-driven signature and no count.
#         harness-gate          run aborts on the multiple-driver check, no property table
#         timeout               proof stops converging (weakest: names no property)
#         none                  NOTHING detects it -- see notes. A `none` row is not a
#                               non-result: it pins a measured green, so a future change
#                               that starts detecting it reports *** CHANGED ***.
#                               All three `none` rows (F-23, F-24, F-26) are RETRACTED
#                               findings, and that is not a coincidence -- a retraction
#                               is exactly what "the suite is green and that is correct"
#                               looks like from inside the sweep. These rows are the
#                               tripwire on each retraction: they are the only thing that
#                               would notice if a future change started detecting a defect
#                               the record says is not there. Leave them out and each
#                               retraction is just a paragraph.
# THE DRIVER CHECKS THE expect FIELD ONLY, and that is deliberate -- decided
# 2026-09-01, not an oversight. The proven/cex counts in the notes are prose and
# are not parsed, so a row can drift from 6 proven/3 cex to 2 proven/7 cex and
# still report CAUGHT. This file is a way to REPRODUCE an issue, not a golden
# transcript of a run: what a row promises is that the named detector still
# fires, and pinning the surrounding counts would fail the sweep on unrelated
# proof progress. Read the counts as context for what you should expect to see,
# not as an assertion.
#finding

TIMEOUT at 600s (ceiling lowered from 1800s 2026-09-01: the row's whole content is that it does NOT converge, and 1800s of wall clock per sweep to re-learn that is not worth it). NOT a sizing artifact: identical tcl, and the control run's slowest property proves in 174s -- ~3.5x headroom at the 600s ceiling, down from ~10x at 1800s. That is a real loss of evidential strength and the reason the ceiling must not go lower: below ~2x, 'did not converge' stops being distinguishable from 'slow'. CI goes red but no property is named.

GREEN 20/0, mutation verified real (3 guards removed). RETRACTED as a defect 2026-09-01; guards KEPT -- same disposition as F-24. expect=none is unchanged but its REASON is now the opposite of what this note used to say. It is NOT 'formal is two-state so the sim half owns this': THE SIM HALF WAS MEASURED AND IS ALSO BLIND. At QUEUE_SIZE=15, instrumented identically, the deepest level is entered 1452 times in BOTH builds and X reaches the comparator inputs 0 times guarded / 2159 times unguarded -- reachable, heavily exercised, genuinely injecting X, and the suite is green anyway because X never reaches o_data and every check watched the port. There is no sim-side detector to write; one was looked for. The RTL settles why: an explicit `parent_lvl == TREE_DEPTH-1` override at the end of the same combinational arm -- PREDATING fe40af5 -- zeroes next_parent_lvl/next_parent_idx and forces both write enables low, so nothing tainted is ever committed. The walk terminates BY DESIGN, not by accident. Synthesis agrees where there is no X at all: Vivado 2025.1 / xcau25p / OOC gives 1272 LUTs guarded vs 1259 unguarded, 789 FF both, same CARRY8, RAM and warnings; the one falsifiable hazard (write aliasing) needs MORE decode logic and the unguarded build has less with identical state, which points away from it. Not a proven equivalence -- different netlists, no LEC. VERI-9005 count is TEN with AND without the guards: that warning is a static width observation a guard does not silence, so it never discriminated. STILL OPEN, and unrelated to the retraction: two level_1[parent_idx] sites are in range only by an invariant the walk maintains and nothing asserts -- worth a white-box property, not written. STALE ARTIFACT: the RTL comment fe40af5 added still claims the walk 'terminated by accident' and cites no F-number, so grepping F-23 will not find it.

GREEN 20/0, guard verified removed. NOT a hole: a_no_placeholder_at_capacity PROVES (28.35s), so the overflow state cannot occur. RETRACTION CANDIDATE: at 1f8dbd3 (F-24's own commit) with bbc3ef2 cherry-picked for a sound RAM, a_occ_bounded and a_queue_size_bounded both PROVE in 60.42s while c_root_placeholder_nonempty still covers. The cex was an F-21 artifact -- the seventh. See LEDGER-RESULTS.

GREEN 20 proven/0 cex/35 covers -- byte-identical to unmodified HEAD. NOTHING detects it. RETRACTED as a defect (F-17's category, the seventh false one) and this row is the tripwire on the retraction: expect=none means a future change that starts detecting it prints *** CHANGED *** and the retraction gets revisited. Not merely unexercised -- the precondition is REACHABLE (c_walk_runs_during_fill and c_walk_dirties_fill both cover in 2 cycles on the reverted design); the corruption simply does not survive to $fell(filling) at QUEUE_SIZE=7, DATA_WIDTH=2. Do NOT add a_walk_parked to manufacture a catch; see LEDGER-RESULTS 'Do NOT use'.

THE ONLY HARNESS-CLASS ROW. 9 asserts proven and 0 cex -- IDENTICAL to a clean run -- beside c_reset_reasserted UNREACHABLE, 'proven unreachable in 0.00 s'. The whole finding is the one cover. Mutates the INSTRUMENT, not the design: it is the only row that tests whether the harness is load-bearing, which is this effort's thesis. Mirror image of F-28, which is the same verdict shape from the design side. Revert is wrong: 17490f9 rewrites eleven other tcl scripts and adds hwpq_rst.sv; the patch restores the pre-harness elaborate/reset pair on ONE module.
